SPACE CRAFT JOURNAL / MEETING & CONFERENCE SPACES

Corporate office interior design ideas for a conference room.

Design for everyone in the conversation. This Space Craft planning note looks at corporate office interior design ideas for a conference room through the choices that affect everyday use, the details worth testing and the questions to take into your project brief.

Space Craft editorialPlanning note · 4 min read
IN THIS NOTEStart with the meeting typesCheck the view from every seatTreat sound and air as design inputsTranslate values into behavioursBefore you decide
01 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Start with the meeting types

Separate short discussions, long workshops and hybrid calls in the brief. The right setting depends on duration, attendance, privacy and the equipment people need to use.

02 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Check the view from every seat

Screens, cameras, writing surfaces and presentation positions should work together. Avoid assuming that a long table automatically offers an equal experience to every participant.

03 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Treat sound and air as design inputs

Review room acoustics, service requirements and likely occupancy with the relevant specialists. A good-looking enclosed room still needs to support conversation and regular use.

04 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Translate values into behaviours

Ask what the business wants people to experience: clarity, openness, craft, energy or calm. Connect these words to planning and material decisions rather than applying them only as slogans.

BEFORE YOU DECIDE

Take this into your brief.

  • List the equipment and connections people need.
  • Check sightlines and camera framing from every seat.
  • Allow for furniture movement and maintenance access.

Write down one priority, one constraint and one question you still need to answer. Review them beside the plan or material sample before agreeing the next design decision.

General design considerations for discussion. Product suitability, technical performance, statutory requirements and project pricing need appropriate, project-specific review. Images are illustrative.
